Mining and transportation of coal will require the consumption of other fossil fuel resources. Currently, the mining of 1,000,000 tons of coal requires about 150,000 gallons of diesel fuel and 5,250,000 kwh of electrical power; shipping the coal requires an estimated 2,000,000 gallons of diesel fuel. Based on these figures, the energy investment is approximately 1.91 percent of the energy recovered.
Physiography and Topography
Mining of the lease tract areas will destroy some aspects of the landscape which lend a picturesque character to this land. The ledges, cliffs and caprocks that create this diversity cannot be recreated, and their loss will significantly decrease the visual interest of the area. Vibration from blasting may also topple formations in adjacent areas. Soils
After mining, the pre-mining stratification of soils now present on the site will no longer exist. Assuming eventual mining of all coal present, about 25,000 acres will be affected. The usable existing topsoil will be scraped from the surface, stockpiled if necessary and replaced on the spoils. Soils are complex inorganic and organic materials, produced by physical and biotic activities. Reestablishment of chemical balances and soil microcommunities is necessary to develop soil structure, permeability, and aeration. The weathering process is necessary to leach the soluble salts downward in the soil profile so that they will not interfere with plant growth. In areas as dry as the project site, this weathering process is quite slow. A long period of time will elapse before the reconstituted soil becomes mature.
